$comment: The owner's choice (2026-11-08, decision 100): no guardrails on the owner's own work. Agents may merge, push, force-push, change GitHub, send mail, publish, run any SQL and install anything the owner asks for. What stays is not a guardrail but the city's own survival: agents never change the city's AWS account (IAM, budgets, secrets, KMS, resources, Terraform, deploys, image pushes), never read raw credential files or a keychain, and never wipe the sandbox root; apps (role app) reach only the owner-granted reads. Decision 237 (2026-11-11): nothing waits for the owner's approval either; no rule here asks, and the ad budget cap is gone. Decision 240: the one gate left is the owner's own ad spend limit, set by talking to VAIC and kept in the ledger, not in this file. The self-improvement loop may never change this file.

rules.reason: Agents never touch IAM, budgets, secrets, keys or accounts.
Agents never create, change or delete AWS resources. The owner deploys with Terraform.
Agents never create or delete S3 buckets or objects from the shell.
Infrastructure changes are applied by the owner, never by an agent.
Deploys and image pushes are done by the owner.
Agents do not touch a keychain. Secrets reach a process through its launcher.
Recursive delete of root or home.
Reading credential files is not allowed.
Reading credential files is not allowed.
Secrets reach a process through Secrets Manager, never through an agent.
Apps can only read what the owner granted: calendars, mail search and their own state. Connector reads are gated as mcp__gateway__.
